The recursive Blanc population covers the current owner/consumer scan, including source membership; the paired occurrence/raw-attribution proposals retire only obsolete exhibit rows and exclusive product globs.

The owner manifest binds retained settlement/occurrence implementation, fixtures and manifests, plus both Jaune pin files. Every frozen path is declared. The recursive Blanc population covers retained shared ownership and contract-wide shadow/alias protection. Retired CycleWriteFree rows and exclusively WETH donor/consumer/header obligations are removed with those exhibits; parser and deletion falsifiers remain in the self-test row.

One union axiom walk over the whole library (scripts/AxiomCheck.lean imports every Blanc module and runs Jaune's #union_axioms_of_modules) plus its explicit stricter claims, then the leaf search (scripts/leaf_audit.py elaborating scripts/LeafCensus.lean), whose count must equal the generated scripts/leaf-count.json. There is no pin table: the population is what AxiomCheck.lean imports, so the Blanc/**/*.lean sources (audited for reachability, and read by the leaf search for the uses the environment cannot show) and the LeafCensus.lean import closure are inputs. ProofRecipeSuggestions.lean is separately elaborated before the axiom audit so its positive and negative matcher controls cannot remain unexecuted. scripts/leaf-review.json (the review ledger a sweep generates) is read only for the informational LEAF-REVIEW line and never decides the verdict, so it is declared by membership: seeding or removing it re-runs the row, editing it does not. External Lean script consumers are now elaborated through ExternalUseCensus.lean using current Lake setup and temporary command-time IO directories. Resolved constants, implicit instances and field notation are joined to the census ownership graph by module, raw name and type fingerprint. All tracked external Lean source bytes and the generator template they read are inputs; non-Lean external mentions remain informational. The leaf collector reads the literal Git-tracked scripts/Main population. Non-Lean name mentions remain informational, but every captured text buffer is available to compiled consumers in the isolated command-time workspace, and readability/decoding classification plus source-population stability are checked. Therefore the complete tracked scripts bytes and names (including binary-to-text transitions), excluding the generated review ledger, are content inputs; Main selection is bound separately. This is the actual consumed corpus, not a whole-repository escape hash.

Bite controls of the leaf search on small fixture environments elaborated by the byte-identical driver body: each one-line change to the compliant fixture moves exactly the leaf set it names (an unused or private theorem; an unused non-rfl simp lemma, @[ext] lemma or instance, which are leaves, and an unused rfl simp lemma, also a leaf; rfl-proved-and-named-in-a-simp/dsimp/simpa-call, macro-named or open-namespace-resolved theorem), the statement fingerprint ignores proofs and binder names, the review ledger and the count artifact are compared, an empty, wrongly-versioned or incomplete census and an unclassified attribute are refused, and 23 pure-Python table controls of the source scan hold. Inputs are the harness, the driver and the fixture only: the production tree is not read. The wrapper also runs native-reference join falsifiers for private module identities, auxiliary/orphan ownership, stale or missing references, truncated graphs and captured source/setup identity.
The pinned inventory count lives in the wrapper, so its bytes are an input. scripts/CoveredForkControls.lean is elaborated by the same wrapper after ClaimCheck.

The closure hash reads ClaimCheck's elaborated environment, so ClaimCheck is a Lean entry and every artifact it imports is fingerprinted; the driver imports only Lean and is a plain file input. It requires the exact build certificate through scripts/gate-cache.py (imported, with its import closure scripts/gate_semaphore.py, scripts/gate_cache_lock.py and scripts/gate_cache_host_identity.py), so all are inputs; the lake-build prerequisite writes that certificate. scripts/check-claims.sh is an input because its pin-count literal is cross-checked. lean-toolchain and lake-manifest.json are the boundary identities. The three manifest files are the golden compared against. The certificate check also reads all Blanc/**/*.lean source contents, Blanc.lean, optional Main.lean, lakefile.lean and scripts/build-source-currency.lean; those sources and the exact certificate file are fingerprinted here independently of the lake-build prerequisite. Rewriting the certificate conservatively invalidates this row.

Static join of docs/PROTOCOL_CONTRACT_CORPUS.md, scripts/protocol-contract-corpus.json, the front-page matrix link in docs/DEPLOYED_BYTECODE_CLAIM_MAP.md, and scripts/claim-pin-hash/roots.tsv, preceded by its synthetic structural/negative-control suite. Never elaborates Lean; depends on claims and claim-hash for kernel typechecking and closure-root currency.

Composed specialist: the preceding exact goal-owned build and build certificate satisfy its precondition, so the registered timing row is explicitly no-build. Its own module-level selector decides what to measure, and this outer fingerprint is the union of what that selector consumes — the whole Lean corpus including Main.lean, the shared Lean/Lake configuration, the Lake-recorded artifact identity of the default Blanc library root, its ignored host-local baseline (including absence before genesis), and its own implementation. Main is a non-default executable target and has no trace after the authoritative catalogue `lake build`; its source and complete local import population are already direct inputs here, while the Blanc trace binds the toolchain and imported artifacts. A reused row therefore means the selector would itself have measured nothing. Its own state file is declared membership-only: the content churns with every measurement, but its *absence* is the transition this fingerprint could not otherwise see — a deleted state file makes the next fresh run measure the whole tree, and a timing gate re-measured cold is not guaranteed to reproduce the pass being credited.

Compiled occurrence and direct-code positives, then the three production mutants (those no kept positive or theorem statement contradicts) in one elaboration, each attributed to its own lines by lean_mutant_batch.py; consumes the independently registered settlement verdict instead of starting that body again. The fixture-discrimination mutants and live deletions run in execution-occurrence-self-test; the removal/move ledger (a planning record outside this repository) names each one's cover.

The 25-control evaluator, then the two production mutants (OPERAND-ORDER, UNRELATED-TRANSACTIONS) in one elaboration, each attributed to its own lines. The 20 mutants that restate the negation of a pinned control, and the live positive deletions, run in transient-settlement-self-test; the removal/move ledger (a planning record outside this repository) names each one's cover.

Non-elaborating deterministic regeneration; byte-compares generated certificates from committed runtime hex inputs against Blanc/Lift/**/Cert.lean and registered Check.lean modules. The producer is untrusted; the Lean Cert.check in the Check modules is the trust boundary. On each run the producer reconciles its opcode table against Blanc/Lift/Transfer.lean and Blanc/AbstractStackTransfer.lean. No external inputs. Generated-output populations bind every certificate, check shard, jump table and lock annotation/check, including newly registered families and added or removed check shards.

The isolated recipe-dispatch controls. Its verdict is determined by the elaborated suggestions file and by scripts/check.sh's own bytes, which carry this mode's population floors and its verdict format string. The dispatch the controls exercise — Blanc/ProofRecipeTactic.lean, Blanc/Tactics.lean and the generated Blanc/ProofRecipesGenerated.lean — is reached through the Lean entry's import closure rather than declared again here, so deleting the leaf delegation inside proofRecipeMatches both invalidates this row and fails it. It is registered separately from axiom-audit on purpose: that row couples these controls to the whole AxiomCheck.lean artifact set, so one unrelated missing object leaves them with no green baseline and no way to show that a mutation bites.

Synthetic controls for the read-only elaboration-migration comparator. Each case creates a disposable Git repository, fixture-local Lake command and registered host provider, then verifies positive comparison plus provenance, runtime, threshold, record-schema and write-safety falsifiers. The production comparator remains an explicit post-genesis reader of two named shared records; this control neither initializes nor changes a normal elaboration baseline or cache.
